podcast.body: Found on the *Stadium Arcadium* album, this song was released about 13 years after Tom Petty's "Mary Jane's Last Dance" and showed significant sonic similarities. The question of whether this was "blatantly and consciously copying Tom Petty" or an "unfortunate Sonic coincidence" was raised, but Tom Petty himself doubted negative intent. "Was this the Chili Peppers blatantly and consciously copying Tom Petty?"

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: Released as part of their album "Stadium Arcadium" on May 9, 2006, this song shared notable sonic similarities with Tom Petty's "Mary Jane's Last Dance" (1993). Despite the similarities, Tom Petty never initiated a lawsuit, though it was suggested he considered it. "The Red Hot Chili Peppers with Danny California from their Stadium Arcadia album, which was released on May 9, 2006."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This single was released from the double-disc album "Stadium Arcadium" on May 5, 2006. The song's success contributed to the album's strong sales of 6.5 million copies, making it a rare highlight for the struggling recording industry in the late 2000s. "The Red Hot Chili Peppers with Danny California, a single from their double disc Stadium Arcadia, which came out on May 5, 2006, and eventually sold about 6.5 million copies by the end of the decade."
